From the reflected corrected GCD, the candidate is \(18\).

For \(y=1\), the expression equals \(18\), so any \(x\) dividing every term must divide \(18\). Thus \(x \le 18\).

Now show \(18\) divides every term. Modulo \(2\):
\[
7^y+12y-1 \equiv 1+0-1 \equiv 0 \pmod 2.
\]
Modulo \(9\):
\[
7^y+12y-1 \equiv (-2)^y+3y-1 \pmod 9.
\]
Check by \(y \bmod 3\):
- If \(y\equiv 0\pmod 3\), \((-2)^y\equiv 1\), \(3y\equiv 0\), so result \(\equiv 0\).
- If \(y\equiv 1\pmod 3\), \((-2)^y\equiv -2\), \(3y\equiv 3\), so result \(\equiv 0\).
- If \(y\equiv 2\pmod 3\), \((-2)^y\equiv 4\), \(3y\equiv 6\), so result \(\equiv 0\).

Thus \(18\) divides \(7^y+12y-1\) for all natural \(y\). Since no larger divisor can divide the \(y=1\) value \(18\), the greatest such \(x\) is

\[
\boxed{18}
\]
